text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko was given a red carpet welcome in Hanoi on Thursday by President Le Duc Anh. The two presidents later agreed that Vietnam and Belarus should strive more to boost bilateral cooperation.
-- A $9.27-million joint venture between France's Total and local company Tradimexco to import, store and market liquefied petroleum gas has been licensed.
-- Vietnam and Hungary, whose Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs is on a four-day visit, see the possibility for an agreement on fighting terrorism, organized crimes and drug trafficking.

-- Businesses established under the law on state-owned enterprises and corporate law and enterprises under social and political organizations will be permitted to provide consulting services for foreign investors.
-- President Le Duc Anh and Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet have accepted an invitation to visit Belarus.
-- The country's first ice-skating rink will be opened on Saturday in Ho Chi Minh City.
-- The customs office reported that exports were $1.9 billion in the first quarter and imports were $2.69 billion.
-- Directors of Ho Chi Minh City's private companies Minh Phung and EPCO, who were arrested last month, are prosecuted with charges of fraud.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's Party Committee has held a meeting to discuss issues of security and national defence, ideologiacl work and policy on party membership.
